result.reason: The closed FCSTM shows root -> PumpControl reachable, but PumpControl's own default entry goes to a compiler-owned UnspecifiedInitial synthetic state (a dead-end leaf), not to PumpState. None of PumpRegion/WaterRegion/MethaneRegion nor PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState is reachable_from_initial=true per inspection_equivalent_facts and verify_facts (all refuted). This drives distinct behavior-consequence issues: (1) PumpControl's owner-local default entry is malformed/missing toward PumpState (NL3 initial_entry contract), (2) the required PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState transition endpoints (NL4/NL5) exist structurally at PumpRegion/WaterRegion/MethaneRegion initial edges but their whole owning regions/states are unreachable from root, which is a root-reachability defect distinct from local endpoint existence, and (3) the reachable leaf UnspecifiedInitial is a genuine deadlock frontier fact but it is compiler-owned synthetic and not an author-specified operating state, so it supports only the initial-entry defect for PumpControl and is not promoted to a separate deadlock_freedom violation against an author-declared operating state. I therefore derive one reachability contract for the PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState substates as root-unreachable operating states (a property NL-only extraction could not see because NL3/4/5 only stated local transition/entry obligations, not their unreachable ancestry), keep the NL3 initial_entry candidate for the malformed/redirected owner-local default edge, and mark the NL4/NL5 transition_endpoints contracts and their containment counterparts as unresolved-not-applicable because the exact PumpState->WaterState and PumpState->MethaneState edges from NL are not present at all in either author source or FCSTM (only initial pseudostate edges into each region exist) which is itself a stronger transition_endpoints defect: I include S2 candidates for the missing PumpState->WaterState and PumpState->MethaneState edges since neither exists in the complete transition inventory (only 5 transitions total: root->PumpControl, PumpControl->UnspecifiedInitial, and three region-local initial edges). NL2-CARD-1 cardinality is handled via cardinality_bindings only, per protocol.

issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the NL's 'can also transition to' describes only a narrative alternative path rather than a literal state-machine edge; however the contract explicitly requires a transition_endpoints fact between two named exact states, and the complete transition inventory contains zero PumpState-sourced edges of any kind.
issues.title: No transition from PumpState to WaterState exists in the exact source or closed transition inventory

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions (no PumpState source); inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions (5 rows, none sourced from PumpState); inspection_equivalent_facts.states PumpState/MethaneState outgoing_transition_refs: [].
issues.expected: A transition from PumpState to MethaneState must exist as the second alternative from PumpState.
issues.observed: The complete exact_source_inventory and closed FCSTM transition inventories contain no PumpState-sourced edge to any target; PumpState (outgoing_transition_refs: []) and MethaneState reside in disjoint sibling regions (PumpRegion, MethaneRegion) each only entered by their own local [*] edge.
issues.reason: Same exact negative-inventory result as NL4-ENDPOINT-1: no PumpState-sourced transition of any kind exists, so the required PumpState->MethaneState edge is confirmed missing from the complete inventory.
issues.requirement_quote: Similarly, the system can transition to the MethaneState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the methane flow.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The narrative could be read as informal scenario description rather than a structural edge requirement, but the contract's typed property is transition_endpoints over two exact named states, and the inventory absence is unambiguous.
issues.title: No transition from PumpState to MethaneState exists in the exact source or closed transition inventory

issues.basis: NL-GROUP-NL3-PUMPSTATE-ALT alternatives ALT-NL4-WATERSTATE/ALT-NL5-METHANESTATE both have event=null, guard=null, observed_transition_ref=null; inspection_equivalent_facts.states PumpState outgoing_transition_refs=[]; exact_source_inventory.transitions has no PumpState-sourced row.
issues.expected: The alternative transitions from PumpState to WaterState and from PumpState to MethaneState must carry distinguishable, mutually exclusive conditions so exactly one is selected per admissible run.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM contains zero transitions sourced from PumpState (outgoing_transition_refs: [] for PumpState in inspection_equivalent_facts.states), so there is no pair of guarded alternatives to compare for disjointness at all; the underlying carrier edges required by NL4/NL5 are both absent from the complete inventory.
issues.reason: guard_disjointness has no registered predicate and, more critically, its two required alternative transitions are both absent from the closed model, so the comparison the NL demands cannot be executed on any real carrier; this is preserved as a predicate-null candidate per protocol rather than omitted.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the PumpControl state, from which it can transition to different substates based on specific conditions.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Because the group's underlying transitions do not exist, one could argue this obligation is vacuously moot rather than violated; however the NL establishes a positive obligation that the alternatives be distinguishable, and their total absence means the required distinguishing structure was never realized, which is itself a precise unsupported-expression/other gap that must remain visible rather than silently dropped.
issues.title: The two condition-selected alternatives from PumpState cannot be compared for guard disjointness because neither transition exists in the closed model

issues.basis: fcstm_model.text: 'state UnspecifiedInitial ...; [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial;' inside PumpControl scope; inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions transition:line:16 source=[*] target=UnspecifiedInitial scope=PumpControl; working_contract elements.compiler_owned lists UnspecifiedInitial as synthetic_state; inspection_equivalent_facts.states PumpRegion reachable_from_initial=false.
issues.expected: PumpControl, as the owner scope, must have its default/initial entry edge lead into PumpState (directly or through PumpRegion) as its first-entered operating substate.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's only PumpControl-owned default edge is [*] -> UnspecifiedInitial (transition:line:16), a compiler-owned synthetic leaf with no outgoing transition; PumpState is never reached by any owner-local entry edge from PumpControl, and PumpRegion itself is reachable_from_initial=false.
issues.reason: NL3 explicitly requires PumpControl to first transition into PumpState. The exact owner (PumpControl) binding hint is violated because PumpControl's actual initial edge targets a different, compiler-synthesized placeholder state, not PumpState or any region containing it.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: PumpRegion does have a correctly formed local initial edge PumpRegion[*] -> PumpState (tr_0002/transition:line:5), so the nested region-local obligation is separately satisfied; however that inner edge cannot satisfy the outer PumpControl-owned first-entry obligation because PumpControl itself never enters PumpRegion at all.
issues.title: PumpControl's owner-local default entry routes to a compiler-owned synthetic UnspecifiedInitial leaf instead of PumpState

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states reachable_from_initial=false for state_ref PumpRegion:line:3, PumpState:line:4, WaterRegion:line:7, WaterState:line:8, MethaneRegion:line:11, MethaneState:line:12; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL entries at lines 3,4,7,8,11,12; verify_facts.checks.non_proved reachability refuted for the same six subject_refs; metrics.reachable_state_count=3 vs state_count=9.
issues.expected: Because NL1-NL5 describe the system actually operating in PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState after entering PumpControl, these three substates and their owning regions must be reachable from the root initial entry in the finite closed model.
issues.observed: PumpControl's only default entry routes to the compiler-owned UnspecifiedInitial leaf; consequently PumpRegion, WaterRegion, MethaneRegion and their substates PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState are all marked reachable_from_initial=false, with matching STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics and refuted verify_facts reachability checks for all six.
issues.reason: This is a cross-view causal consequence not visible from the individual NL4/NL5 endpoint or containment contracts alone: even if the PumpState->WaterState/MethaneState edges existed, the entire branch is unreachable from root because PumpControl's default entry bypasses all three regions in favor of a synthetic placeholder. The narrower endpoint and containment contracts do not state this global reachability property, so it is captured by this derived contract per the frontier discipline on required wrappers/regions absent from root reachability.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the PumpControl state, from which it can transition to different substates based on specific conditions.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: Each region does contain a locally well-formed initial pseudostate edge into its own substate ([*] -> PumpState inside PumpRegion, etc.), so in isolation each region's internal entry semantics are individually correct; the defect is purely that PumpControl never enters any of these regions, not that the region-local edges are malformed.
issues.title: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState (and their owning regions) are unreachable from the closed model root
